name: Fallen Towers
description: Pizano built an array $$$a$$$ of $$$n$$$ towers, each consisting of $$$a_i \ge 0$$$ blocks. Pizano can knock down a tower so that the next $$$a_i$$$ towers grow by $$$1$$$. In other words, he can take the element $$$a_i$$$, increase the next $$$a_i$$$ elements by one, and then set $$$a_i$$$ to $$$0$$$. The blocks that fall outside the array of towers disappear. If Pizano knocks down a tower with $$$0$$$ blocks, nothing happens. Pizano wants to knock down all $$$n$$$ towers in any order, each exactly once . That is, for each $$$i$$$ from $$$1$$$ to $$$n$$$, he will knock down the tower at position $$$i$$$ exactly once. Moreover, the resulting array of tower heights must be non-decreasing . This means that after he knocks down all $$$n$$$ towers, for any $$$i \lt j$$$, the tower at position $$$i$$$ must not be taller than the tower at position $$$j$$$. You are required to output the maximum $$$\text{MEX}$$$ of the resulting array of tower heights. The $$$\text{MEX}$$$ of an array is the smallest non-negative integer that is not present in the array.
input_specification: Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line contains the number of test cases $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \le t \le 10^4$$$). The description of the test cases follows. The first line of each test case contains an integer $$$n$$$ ($$$1 \leq n \leq 10^5$$$) — the number of towers. The second line of each test case contains $$$n$$$ integers — the initial heights of the towers $$$a_1, \ldots, a_n$$$ ($$$0 \leq a_i \leq 10^9$$$). It is guaranteed that the sum of $$$n$$$ over all test cases does not exceed $$$10^5$$$.
output_specification: For each test case, output a single integer — the maximum $$$\text{MEX}$$$ of the final array.
approach_summary: Verify predicate monotonicity: P(x) is true for x ≤ K and false otherwise. Binary search over the answer domain to find the boundary in O(log(Range) × Verify_Time).

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 2108F — Fallen Towers [33. Binary Search]
topic_editorial.summary: Binary search on the monotonic answer domain.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The predicate function $P(x)$ ('Is answer $\le x$ feasible?') is monotonic: if $P(x)$ is true for some value, it remains true for all larger values (or vice versa). This allows binary division of the answer search space $[\text{low}, \text{high}]$ in $O(\log(\text{Range}))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N \log(\text{Range}))$
  The binary search divides the search interval by 2 at each iteration, requiring $\log_2(\text{Range})$ steps. In each step, the feasibility check `check(mid)` scans the array in $\mathcal{O}(N)$ time.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(1)$ auxiliary space
  The algorithm operates directly over the input array without allocating extra auxiliary memory.
